title: Frightful's Mountain (Selected Chapters & The Return to the Wild)
author: Jean Craighead George
citation: George, Jean Craighead. Frightful's Mountain. Dutton Children's Books, 1999.

sections.heading: Imprinted on Sam: The Call of the Wild Catskills

epigraph.quote: Frightful was a peregrine falcon, born to ride thermals at two hundred miles an hour. But her heart was bound to a boy in the hemlock tree.

paragraphs: In the third installment of Jean Craighead George's beloved wilderness saga that began with My Side of the Mountain, the story shifts point of view to Frightful, Sam Gribley's majestic peregrine falcon. Hand-raised and trained by Sam in the Catskill Mountains, Frightful is 'imprinted' on human beings. She knows Sam's voice, trusts his gloved fist, and looks to him for food.

However, because holding a bird of prey without a master falconer's license is illegal under New York conservation law, conservation officers confiscate Frightful and release her into the wild. Frightful finds herself thrust onto the rocky cliffs of Delhi, New York, completely unequipped for the instinctual demands of wild survival: reading weather thermals, hunting evasive prey without human cues, and recognizing dangerous predators.

sections.heading: Migration, Peregrine Recovery, and Environmental Threats

epigraph.quote: There is a one-ness of all things: the falcon, the hemlock, the river, and the wind.

paragraphs: Through evocative, scientifically accurate prose, George portrays Frightful's gradual awakening to her ancient falcon heritage. Guided by deep genetic memory and encounters with wild tiercels (male falcons) like Chup and 426, Frightful learns to dive ('stoop') at blistering speeds exceeding two hundred miles per hour, navigate the Appalachian flyway, and foster abandoned eyases (falcon chicks).

Throughout her journeys, Frightful faces the harsh environmental realities threatening raptors: high-voltage power lines, poachers seeking rare eggs, and the historical legacy of pesticides like DDT that once drove peregrine falcons to the brink of extinction across North America. Frightful's triumphant return to wild independence stands as a celebrated symbol of ecological conservation and human stewardship.
